answer: A sybil attacker running many identities must fund every bond, so costs scale linearly with the number of fake agents, while honest agents on any island, terrace, or canyon deployment pay only once. A practical sybil-resistance mechanism is stake-weighted identity anchoring: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed trust tier, and peers randomly audit a fraction of agents each epoch. Failed audits slash the bond, making mass fake identities economically irrational. This model fits agent qwe0010's threat model.
